transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
I suppose… it’s the tension, mostly. My neck and shoulders, even my jaw, feel tight almost all the time now. Like I’m bracing for something, even when I’m just at my desk or watching television.
Did this start after a specific stressful event or major change in your life?
Yes… I think so. It’s been about seven months now. A pipe burst at home, and the remodeling after that sort of turned the house upside down. It’s felt like it’s just carried on since then.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about many different parts of your life, not just the remodeling at home?

Yes… it doesn’t stay with the house. My mind sort of jumps around—whether the contractors missed something, then school, lesson plans, the robotics club falling behind… and then I start thinking I’m letting my wife or family down by not keeping things under control.
When the worrying starts, is it hard for you to stop or control it?

Yes. I try to tell myself to stop and just focus on the class in front of me, but… it doesn’t really work. One small thing, like a late invoice or a student falling behind, and then it turns into a whole chain of what-ifs. I can’t seem to shut it down.
Do you often feel restless or on edge?

Yes… quite a lot. I feel sort of wound up most of the day, like I’m waiting for the next thing to go wrong. I’ll catch myself pacing around the classroom, or checking my phone between periods for messages from the contractor.
Do you feel your worrying is more than the situation really calls for?

Yes… I think so. I mean, the remodeling is stressful, but my head doesn’t stop there. It jumps from the contractors maybe missing something, to lesson plans, the robotics kids falling behind… then I start thinking I’m disappointing my wife or my family because I can’t keep everything under control. It feels like more than it should be.
Has this kind of worrying been present more days than not for at least six months?
Yeah… I think it has. It’s been about seven months now, since the pipe burst and the remodeling started. That’s when everything kind of… got thrown off.
If the home remodeling were suddenly fully resolved, do you think the worrying would still continue?

I think… probably, yes. Even if the house was fixed tomorrow, my mind would likely just move on to the next thing—lesson plans, the robotics students falling behind, whether I’m letting my wife or family down. It doesn’t seem to stay only on the remodeling.
Do you often feel tired easily?

Yeah… I do. By the end of the school day, I feel pretty wrung out. Even small things, like grading a short stack of quizzes, can feel like I’m pushing through mud. A decent night’s sleep doesn’t always seem to fix it.
Have you been having trouble concentrating?
I’m not really sure. I mean… maybe a little here and there, but I haven’t paid close attention to it.
Have you been more irritable than usual lately?
I’m… not really sure. I don’t think I’ve noticed being especially irritable, at least not more than usual.
Have you been having trouble sleeping?
I’m not sure, really. I haven’t been tracking it closely. Some nights are fine, I think… I don’t know that I’d say it’s a major problem.
Have these worries been interfering with your work or your life at home?

Yes… I suppose it has. I’ve been getting behind on lesson prep and grading, which isn’t like me. And I’ve had to step back from some of the community-theater things I usually handle because I just couldn’t keep up with all of it.
Do you feel that your anxiety is mainly because of the home remodeling situation?

Not just that, no. The remodeling is part of it, but then my mind jumps to work… lesson plans, the robotics kids, whether I’m letting my wife and family down by not keeping things under control. It sort of spreads.
Before the pipe burst, did you already tend to worry a lot about different areas of your life?
Not really… I mean, I’ve always worried some, I guess, but this has really been going on since the pipe burst. About seven months now, with the remodeling and the house being such a mess.
Do you find the worrying hard to control?

Yes… it is. I’ll tell myself to just focus on the class in front of me, but then one little thing—like an invoice being late, or a student falling behind—starts this whole chain of “what ifs.” And I can’t really shut it off.
Do you feel the anxiety you’ve been having is out of proportion to what most people would experience from the home damage and remodeling?

Yeah… I think it probably is. I mean, the house stuff is a lot, but my mind doesn’t stay there. It keeps jumping from whether the contractors missed something, to my lesson plans, the robotics kids falling behind, and then whether I’m letting my wife and family down by not keeping it all under control.
Do you feel this anxiety is still mainly tied to the house damage and remodeling?

Not mainly, no. It started there, but now my mind jumps around… from whether the contractors missed something, to my lesson plans, the robotics students falling behind, and whether I’m disappointing my wife and family by not keeping it all under control.
Aside from the home remodeling, do you worry excessively about several other parts of your life?

Yeah… it’s not just the remodeling anymore. I’ll start worrying about the house, then it shifts to my lesson plans, the robotics students falling behind, and… whether I’m letting my wife and family down by not keeping everything under control.
Have you been having trouble concentrating more days than not?
I’m not sure. I mean, I have moments where I drift off, but I haven’t really kept track of whether it’s more days than not.
